metadata.title: How to Make Potato Gratin - The Basics on QVC
metadata.description:
https://qvc.co/recipeideas - Potato gratin! Blue Jean Chef Meredith Laurence teaches you how to make potato gratin. 

Watch more dinner recipe ideas:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL-MJ2niVMKch_9XrwCKpf1A3J3RxEpfj4

Download free recipes from Chef Meredith Laurence:
https://qvc.co/recipeideas 

Follow Blue Jean Chef on Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/bluejeanchef

Potato Gratin
Serves 4 to 6

Ingredients:
2 to 2½ cups half-and-half, divided
2 cloves of garlic, smashed flat
½ teaspoon salt
freshly ground black pepper
¼ teaspoon ground nutmeg
2 pounds potatoes (about 5 or 6), peeled and sliced (¼-inch slices)
1 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 tablespoon butter, cut into small cubes
fresh thyme leaves (optional)

Directions: 
1. Pre-heat the oven to 350˚ F.
2. Combine 1½ cups of half-and-half with the garlic in a shallow skillet or gratin pan and bring to a simmer on the stovetop. Simmer for 15 minutes. Season with the salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
3. Turn the heat off underneath the half-and-half and add the sliced potatoes, separating the slices and pressing them into the half-and-half to ensure they are all distributed evenly. Add enough of the remaining half-and-half to just cover all the potatoes. Top with the Parmesan cheese, dot with butter, and transfer the pan to the oven.
4. Bake in the oven for 50 to 60 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender and nicely browned on top. Serve with a little fresh thyme on top if desired.

nodes.plm_caption: This video shows a demonstration of how to make potatos. A person is holding a potato and has a stove with a pan in the foreground. In the background, we can see a window. towards the end of the video, we can see three small bowls.

summary.brief: A woman in a denim shirt prepares, bakes, and garnishes a creamy potato gratin.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the chef introducing the potato gratin, showing the recommended pan size and the type of potatoes to use. She selects russet potatoes, displays peeled and unpeeled examples, and slices them with a slicer into uniform quarter‑inch rounds. She turns on a skillet, pours about one and a half cups of half‑and‑half into the pan, adds a smashed garlic clove, and brings the mixture to a gentle simmer while seasoning it with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. After fifteen minutes she turns off the heat, folds the sliced potatoes into the hot cream, ensuring each slice is coated, and adds a little more half‑and‑half just to cover the potatoes. She layers the potatoes evenly, sprinkles grated Parmesan cheese over the top, dots the surface with small cubes of butter, and places the skillet in a pre‑heated 350 °F oven. The gratin bakes for roughly fifty to sixty minutes until the potatoes are tender and the surface turns deep golden‑brown. Once removed she inserts a fork to check tenderness, lets the dish rest briefly, then garnishes with fresh thyme leaves, a grind of black pepper, and a little extra Parmesan before serving.

action.detailed: Simmer half‑and‑half with garlic and seasonings, fold in sliced potatoes, top with Parmesan and butter, bake until golden brown, then garnish with thyme, pepper and extra cheese before serving.
action.actor: The chef, a woman wearing a denim shirt with short dark hair

nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a woman with short, dark hair wearing a dark denim shirt as she demonstrates how to grate potatoes using a blue potato grater. She is standing in a kitchen with wooden cabinets and a window, and the background shows a blue frying pan, a bowl of chopped vegetables, and other kitchen appliances.
The woman is talking to the camera the entire video while performing actions with the grater and holding a potato. A visual of the end product is shown at one point and a close-up shot of the potato she is holding.
There is text that moves across the bottom of the screen throughout the video. It says, "THE BASICS POTATO GRATIN" at 1s, "USE A WIDE PAN LESS THAN 2 DEEP" at 3s, and "2 POUNDS PEELED POTATOES" at 7s. In the top right of the screen is another text that says "MED-HI HEAT" at 9s.
The video is well lit, in color, and of high quality, with many clear shots of the objects in the scene. The video is edited well to move smoothly between shots of the woman and the background. The video is also zoomed in at the right moment with the text in the center of the shot.

summary.brief: Meredith Laurence introduces the basics of potato gratin, showing a blue potato grater, the ideal shallow pan, and the amount of peeled potatoes needed.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Meredith Laurence, a short‑haired woman in a dark denim shirt with rolled‑up sleeves, standing at a wooden kitchen counter. She holds a raw potato in her left hand and looks directly at the camera while lower‑third graphics display “THE BASICS POTATO GRATIN.” A blue potato grater rests on the countertop, and she briefly demonstrates how to grate the potato. She then gestures toward a blue frying pan on the stove, taps the pan with a fingertip, and on‑screen text appears reading “USE A WIDE PAN LESS THAN 2 DEEP.” She points to a bowl of peeled potatoes that is later shown, accompanied by the caption “2 POUNDS PEELed POTATOES.” Throughout the segment the background shows a wooden wall, a window with plants, and various kitchen utensils, all illuminated by bright natural light.

action.detailed: Hold a raw potato, speak to the camera, point to the blue frying pan, tap the pan, and display on‑screen text about using a wide shallow pan and the required peeled potatoes while briefly showing a blue potato grater.
action.actor: Meredith Laurence, the Blue Jean Chef

nodes.plm_caption: The video features a woman demonstrating how to make a potato gratin. She starts by pouring milk into a saucepan then starts chopping garlic and loading potatoes into a ruffle slicer. She layering the potatoes into the mixture in a pan. She then adds seasoning before layering the sliced potatoes on top. Finally, she adds butter and puts the pan in the oven before taking it out and breaking the potatos. The video is a food segment from a cooking show.

summary.brief: The chef simmers half‑and‑half with garlic, layers seasoned sliced potatoes in the cream, tops with Parmesan and butter, bakes the gratin, and finishes with thyme, extra cheese and pepper.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the chef heating half‑and‑half and a smashed garlic clove in a skillet until it simmers, then turning the heat off and seasoning the liquid with salt, pepper and nutmeg. She slices the potatoes into uniform quarter‑inch rounds, adds them to the hot cream, and pours enough of the remaining half‑and‑half to just cover the slices, pressing them down. She layers the potatoes, sprinkles grated Parmesan and dots small pieces of butter, repeats another layer of potatoes and cream, and places the pan in a pre‑heated 350 °F oven. After the top turns golden brown and the potatoes are tender, she removes the pan, lets it cool briefly, then garnishes with fresh thyme leaves, a bit more Parmesan cheese and a pinch of black pepper.

action.detailed: Layer sliced potatoes into the garlic‑infused half‑and‑half, season, add enough remaining half‑and‑half to cover, press down, sprinkle Parmesan and butter, repeat the layers, bake in a pre‑heated oven until golden and tender, then garnish with thyme, extra cheese and pepper.
action.actor: The presenter – a woman in a blue denim shirt with short dark hair (the Blue Jean Chef).

summary.brief: The chef simmers a garlic‑flavored half‑and‑half sauce, layers seasoned potato slices with cheese and butter, bakes the gratin until golden, then checks for doneness.
summary.detailed: In a bright kitchen, a woman in a blue shirt turns on a pan, pours 1½ cups of half‑and‑half into it and adds a smashed garlic clove, then brings the mixture to a gentle simmer for about fifteen minutes. She turns the heat off and seasons the cream with salt, freshly ground black pepper and a pinch of grated nutmeg. Thinly sliced potatoes are folded into the hot cream, and enough remaining half‑and‑half is added to just cover the slices. She begins layering the potatoes in the pan, sprinkling grated Parmesan cheese and dotting small cubes of butter between each layer, pressing the slices down to create even layers. Once the pan is fully layered, she transfers it to a pre‑heated 350 °F oven and bakes until the top turns a deep golden brown and a knife inserted in several spots meets little resistance, indicating tenderness. After removing the pan, she pokes the gratin with a paring knife to confirm it is cooked through and lets it rest briefly.

action.detailed: Layer the seasoned potato slices in the simmered half‑and‑half mixture, sprinkle grated Parmesan and dot butter between layers, then bake in a pre‑heated oven until the top is golden brown and the potatoes are tender, and finally test for doneness with a knife.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
https://qvc.co/recipeideas - Potato gratin! Blue Jean Chef Meredith Laurence teaches you how to make potato gratin. 

Watch more dinner recipe ideas:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL-MJ2niVMKch_9XrwCKpf1A3J3RxEpfj4

Download free recipes from Chef Meredith Laurence:
https://qvc.co/recipeideas 

Follow Blue Jean Chef on Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/bluejeanchef

Potato Gratin
Serves 4 to 6

Ingredients:
2 to 2½ cups half-and-half, divided
2 cloves of garlic, smashed flat
½ teaspoon salt
freshly ground black pepper
¼ teaspoon ground nutmeg
2 pounds potatoes (about 5 or 6), peeled a
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with the chef introducing the potato gratin, showing the recommended pan size and the type of potatoes to use. She selects russet potatoes, displays peeled and unpeeled examples, and slices them with a slicer into uniform quarter‑inch rounds. She turns on a skillet, pours about one and a half cups of half‑and‑half into the pan, adds a smashed garlic clove, and brings the mixture to a gentle simmer while seasoning it with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. After fifteen minutes she turns off the heat, folds the sliced potatoes into the hot cream, ensuring each slice is coated, and adds a little more half‑and‑half just to cover the potatoes. She layers the potatoes evenly, sprinkles grated Parmesan cheese over the top, dots the surface with small cubes of butter, and places the skillet in a pre‑heated 350 °F oven. The gratin bakes for roughly fifty to sixty minutes until the potatoes are tender and the surface turns deep golden‑brown. Once removed she inserts a fork to check tenderness, lets the dish rest briefly, then garnishes with fresh thyme leaves, a grind of black pepper, and a little extra Parmesan before serving.

Explain pan choice and slice potatoes uniformly

   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks

     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
